# the contributor audit: the larger-positive omitted-index simplex corollary

Source: `candidate fdab4307532951f8`. Independent root audit: PASS. Scope is exactly two strictly positive heights, omission of the larger positive vertex, arbitrary many negative and zero heights, and a proper section.

The independent exponential representation gives mu_i=d b_i. A coefficient-zero exponential remains independent under section conditioning and has mean one, so deleting zero phases and restoring them preserves the actual d-factor product exactly. The two-positive survival and density formulas yield the displayed F, f, mu_q, and negative-coordinate means. Substitution gives product_{i!=p}mu_i=(X/h)L and the exact variance-gap factorization (X/h)(L-R). The all-m scalar theorem is now fully proved and independently audited, and X/h>0, giving strictness for p>q without a centroid centrality condition.

At p=q, the coarea integral obtained by eliminating the p-coordinate has fixed cone W>=qY_q. Its exponential factor is at most exp(-sum remaining variables), and the inserted conditional coordinates are bounded by a fixed multiple of their sum on a compact positive-p interval. This supplies the stated integrable first-moment dominator. Density at zero remains positive; thus every mu_i and F converges and gives the nonstrict limit. Symmetry allows either tied positive index. Strictness is not claimed merely from strict approximants.

The smaller-positive interface is a separate identity. Its coefficient (1-h)C0 differs from the completed L factor, and the altered h-dependence prevents transferring the critical-location proof automatically. No other omitted index, all-coordinate product, arbitrary sign pattern, general convex body, or mixed-integer statement is inferred.
